name: SDN Host Node Status
description: Capability node for the host read-only node_status_read hostcall (M1 node-status flow, GET /api/v1/node/status). One method, one hostcall: 'status' takes the routing-decision JSON from foundation/http-route route_node_status on port "decision" and, when route=="status", forwards an EMPTY payload ({}) to the node_status_read.status hostcall (capability name IS the op prefix — no capPrefixFromName mapping exists for node_status_read) and emits the hostcall's "result" object VERBATIM as UTF-8 JSON bytes on "body"; the incoming decision is re-emitted unchanged on "decision" (linear flow chaining into foundation/http-respond). Result shape: {uptime_seconds,started_at,store:{total_bytes,total_records,storage_path},disk:{capacity_bytes,free_bytes,available_bytes}|null,service:{state,mode,autostart_known},bandwidth:{total_in_bytes,total_out_bytes,rate_in_bps,rate_out_bps,history:[...]}|null} — an OBJECT (a live status snapshot), not an SDS record collection, so the bare-array JSON convention used by the other gateway flows does not apply here. A decision this method does not own (already rewritten to route=error by the route node, e.g. 405 for non-GET) short-circuits: NO hostcall, the decision passes through untouched and no body frame is pushed — foundation/http-respond owns that response. A node_status_read.status hostcall FAILURE (or a missing/non-object result field) rewrites the decision to route=error status=503 with the host's error message (or an honest fallback) — never a silent empty body. FlatBuffers: there is no SDS schema for node status (checked spacedatastandards.org/schema — no STA/HLT/NOD/SVC-style match exists); a hand-written FlatBuffers table would violate the generated-types-only rule, so v1 ships JSON-ONLY. Anonymity: the $HTQ envelope (module-sdk schemas/HttpRequestAbi.fbs) carries no caller-trust field the flow can read, so this node cannot shape an anonymous subset — the mounted route is declared anonymous:false (operator-gated at the host's auth wall) until the envelope carries trust information.

externalInterfaces.description: Policy-mediated read-only host node-status snapshot (uptime, storage totals, disk, service state, bandwidth counters/history).

acceptedTypeSets.description: Routing-decision JSON frame from foundation/http-route route_node_status: {"route":"status","format":"json"} or {"route":"error","status":405,...} for a non-GET request.

inputPorts.description: One routing-decision JSON frame per request.

acceptedTypeSets.description: The decision forwarded verbatim on success or on routes this method does not own, or rewritten to route=error status=503 when the node_status_read.status hostcall fails or returns no result object.

UTF-8 JSON OBJECT bytes: the node_status_read.status hostcall's "result" object verbatim ({uptime_seconds,started_at,store,disk,service,bandwidth}). NOT a bare array — a single live-status object, not an SDS record collection. Absent on error / not-owned-route decisions.

outputPorts.description: Response body for foundation/http-respond (absent on error decisions).

methods.description: Forwards {} to the node_status_read.status hostcall when route=="status" and emits the raw result object verbatim on "body" plus the decision passthrough on "decision"; routes this method does not own pass through with no hostcall; hostcall failure or a missing result object rewrites the decision to an honest route=error status=503. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is now ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a node that read ordinal 0 of a port and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed there, with nothing re-delivering them and nothing logging the loss (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is now refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.
